sources.title: GPT-6 Astra Model
claims: Standard rates: input 10, cached input 1, output 50 USD per million tokens.
Context 1050000; maximum output 128000; effort low/medium/high/xhigh/max.
Input over 272000 tokens doubles input/cache rates and multiplies output rate by 1.5 for the full request.
Only the gpt-6-astra alias was exposed in the inspected snapshots section.
limits: No account access, throughput or task success was measured.

sources.title: GPT-6.1 Terra Model
claims: Standard rates: input 1, cached input 0.05, output 5 USD per million tokens.
Context 1050000; maximum output 128000; efforts none/low/medium/high/xhigh/max.
Same documented long-context multipliers and tier limits as Astra.
Tool calling requires Responses API.
Only the gpt-6.1-terra alias was exposed in the inspected snapshots section.
limits: Capabilities require task-specific qualification; no exact job acceptance rate follows.

sources.title: Reasoning models
sources.locator: Reasoning mode; How reasoning works; Controlling costs

sources.title: OpenAI API Pricing
claims: Astra 30-minute/12-hour cache writes cost 12.5/25 USD per million tokens; Terra 1.25/2.5.

Batch/Flex half Standard; Fast twice Standard; no such discount assumed in primary study.
limits: Prices do not cover all local infrastructure or enterprise operations.

sources.title: Using GPT-6

sources.title: An Interpretable Automated Mechanism Design Framework with Large Language Models
claims: Mechanism-code search with problem-specific correction provides a direct technical precedent.
Reported known-theory recovery and distribution-overfitting require strong no-sharing baselines and fresh tests.
limits: Specialized supplied fixes are part of the system. No Astra task success, commercial demand or complete enterprise costs measured.

sources.title: SkillsBench: Benchmarking How Well Agent Skills Work Across Diverse Tasks
claims: 87 tasks,18 model-harness configurations; curated skills average pass33.9% to50.5%, gain16.6 percentage points.
Focused packages outperform larger bundles in this benchmark.
limits: Curated skill effect is not self-invention or Astra mechanism-work evidence.

sources.title: SWE-Skills-Bench: Do Agent Skills Actually Help in Real-World Software Engineering?
claims: 39 of49 skills yield no pass-rate improvement; reported average gain1.2%.
Some skills increase token use by451% without improving pass rates; version mismatch can harm.
limits: Supports redundant/harmful-transfer scenarios, not a universal expected gain.

sources.title: From Raw Experience to Skill Consumption: A Systematic Study of Model-Generated Agent Skills
claims: Across five agentic domains, average benefit coexists with negative transfer; extractor and consumer strengths differ.
limits: No justified invariant benefit across models, tasks or skill formats.

sources.title: Nine Judges, Two Effective Votes: Correlated Errors Undermine LLM Evaluation Panels
claims: Nine frontier judges from seven families supplied roughly two independent votes in the reported NLI evaluation.
Common mistakes materially reduced the independent-vote benefit.
limits: Do not transfer its numerical correlation to mechanism correctness; use it to motivate broad common-cause stress.

sources.title: One Skill Too Many: How Co-Installed Skills Conflict in Coding Agents
claims: Co-installed similar skills can displace behavior and lose exclusive functions without lowering task completion.
limits: Access/discovery does not imply safe simultaneous use; scope and policy compatibility require separate evaluation.

sources.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
claims: An executable skill library and feedback loop supports transfer to new Minecraft tasks.
limits: Minecraft evidence supports architecture plausibility only, not commercial or frontier-agent calibration.

sources.title: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
claims: Evaluator-guided code evolution produced reported scientific and infrastructure improvements.
limits: Different models, resources and problems; no economic success probability is transferred.

sources.title: Automating Mechanism Design with Program Synthesis
claims: Programmatic mechanism synthesis with user-defined behavioral assumptions was evaluated in two domains.
limits: Finite model assumptions bound correctness and strategic claims.

sources.title: Using lightweight formal methods to validate a key-value storage node in Amazon S3
claims: The authors report lightweight formal-methods validation of an evolving production storage node using executable reference models and checks matched to different properties.
limits: Primary technical precedent for a deferred venture; not evidence of fully automated delivery, matched project price or Astra task success.

sources.title: Compositional Synthesis of Modular Systems (Full Version)
claims: Per-process implementations and interface certificates enable separate requirements in a compositional synthesis method.
Reported performance advantage depends on reasonably small certificates.
limits: Existing method belongs in the competent Beta reference; does not calibrate customer demand, frontier success or transfer economics.

sources.title: Multiparty Computation from Somewhat Homomorphic Encryption
claims: The proposed multiparty-computation protocol separates preprocessing independent of inputs/function from online execution under a specified adversary model.
limits: Motivates only a deferred public/synthetic protocol-compiler opportunity.
Historical timings are not current cost calibration; identity or synthetic functional checks do not establish cryptographic security.

prohibited_inferences: A benchmark pass rate equals customer acceptance.
A missing skill file means a recipient lacks the underlying knowledge.
Two same-model judgments are independent evidence.
An on-chain commitment establishes usefulness or evidence truth.
Published hourly rates establish project hours, willingness to pay or human-only work.
More graph entries, agents or descendants establish independent invention or compounding.
A subscription price supports unbounded API production.
Positive modeled margin relative to a human-service price establishes Alpha.
A correct or admitted artifact automatically creates positive complete-cost recipient benefit.
A prior Alpha assessment remains current after its Beta version changes.
Known-method local operation counts establish frontier model invention or dollar delivery cost.

conceptual_definitions.beta: Versioned competent frontier reasoning, tools, standard methods, correction and ordinary accumulated recipient experience, including already held equivalent capabilities.
conceptual_definitions.alpha: Supported positive complete-cost increment over versioned Beta and current recipient capabilities in a declared scope; assessment status must distinguish measured, modeled, unresolved and nonpositive.
conceptual_definitions.commercial_reference: Matched human-delivered service; Beta is an internal causal control, not an external AI-market price benchmark.
conceptual_definitions.moving_beta: A baseline version change invalidates the freshness of an earlier Alpha assessment until reassessment; correctness, permissions and current economic increment remain distinct.
hypotheses: Halpha: candidate or bundle increment above strong Beta
Hshare: network sharing increment above isolated retention
Hdurability: persistence or erosion under moving Beta
